item.title: About Fabio
item.description:
While a board of biohackers and stakeholders is being formed, here is who is behind how the project started.

Fabio Pietrosanti — online as naif — started Hacking Biology, and writes everything on this blog. He has spent close to thirty years building things people have to be able to trust, across a run of companies and non-profits that keeps landing in the same place: take a domain nobody has made properly transparent, build the open infrastructure for it, and give it away.

item.title: hackingbiology.com becomes the Foundation's site
item.description:
hackingbiology.com has left WordPress.com. The site is now a static, open build whose entire source — content, layout and history — lives in a public repository .

The reason is the same one that governs everything else here: the Foundation asks people to trust an open platform with their health record, so its own publishing should be inspectable rather than sitting inside someone’s hosted account.

item.title: The Foundation
item.description: Hacking Biology is a non-profit foundation. Its job is narrow and permanent: to own biohack.it and to guarantee the properties the community has to be able to trust — for longer than any individual’s interest in the project.

item.title: Hacking Biology at the Fund Longevity rally in Rome
item.description: Hacking Biology took part in the Fund Longevity global rally on Wednesday 8 April 2026, in Rome, at Largo di Torre Argentina (Via San Nicola de’ Cesarini), 17:00–18:00 CEST. Rome was one of about twenty cities holding a simultaneous action — Amsterdam, Berlin, Brussels, London, Madrid, Paris, Prague, Stockholm, Tel Aviv, Toronto, San Francisco, Abu Dhabi and others — under one banner: fundlongevity.org .

item.title: Glucose and Rapamycin for Anti-Aging
item.description: It’s pretty clear that aging slowdown is directly related to the reduction of glucose in our blood and that Type-II diabetics drugs, almost all, bring in mammal experimentation a lifespan increase (Metformin, GLP-1 inhibitors such as Semaglutide/Liraglutide and Acarbose)

item.description:

item.title: Software Review
item.description:
This page aim to collect an unstructured, later to become structured, review and list of software and software libraries that can be used to:

  • Manage collection of exams results (Simple and elaborated Biomarkers)
  • Manage the ongoing tracking of multiple sampling over time
  • Collect therapeutics used in a research and/or DIY protocol

The mapping is done by analyzing both proprietary and free (open source) software, including SAAS (software as a service) and ones to be installed.
